_comment: Golden corpus for check-commit-message.py. Every consuming repo can run this same corpus against the revision it has pinned, which is how behavioural drift is detected. 'file' mode = commit-msg hook semantics (autosquash allowed); 'range_subject' = CI range semantics (autosquash rejected). Expected is the process exit code.

cases.name: uppercase_type_rejected
cases.why: release-please's real grammar is case-sensitive even though the CC spec says types are case-insensitive; we match the tool, not the spec

cases.name: unknown_type_rejected
cases.why: an unknown type that reached a real main branch before this gate existed

cases.name: github_revert_button_rejected
cases.why: release-please's parser cannot read button-revert subjects either; org convention is manual revert(scope): ...

cases.name: long_subject_accepted
cases.why: deliberate: no length rule; commitlint defaults to 100 but release-please has no limit — documented gap, not an oversight

cases.name: fixup_accepted_in_file_mode
cases.why: autosquash artifact; blocking it breaks git commit --fixup / rebase --autosquash

cases.name: fixup_rejected_in_range_mode
cases.why: a fixup! escaping to a validated range means the autosquash was forgotten

cases.name: breaking_footer_exact_accepted
cases.input:
feat: x

BREAKING CHANGE: api removed

cases.name: breaking_footer_wrong_case_rejected
cases.input:
feat: x

Breaking change: api removed
cases.why: would ship a breaking change as a silent minor/patch bump — worse than the failure this gate exists for

cases.name: breaking_footer_plural_rejected
cases.input:
feat: x

BREAKING CHANGES: api removed

cases.name: body_parens_accepted
cases.input:
fix: x

measured on 2026-08-07 (60 commits) and (parens) are fine
cases.why: locks in the retirement of the old no-parens-in-body rule

cases.name: custom_type_via_types_flag
cases.why: per-repo vocabulary comes through --types, never by editing the script
